title: Two concurrent 'add item' calls create two cart lines for one product
symptom: Checkout (and the order made from it) ends up with two lines for the same variant, each with the requested quantity.
root_cause: Input lines are matched to existing lines before the row lock is taken, so two overlapping requests both decide 'no line yet' and both insert.
trigger: Two checkoutLinesAdd requests for the same variant overlap in time (double click, client retry).
why_missed: The function does take a lock, so it looks safe; the decision that matters was made earlier, outside it.
fix_summary: Re-match input lines against the lines read under the lock, inside the transaction.
pattern: check-then-act: decision computed before the lock, acted on after it
reproduction_needs: two requests interleaved at a chosen point
fixed:
_match_lines_data_to_locked_lines(checkout_lines_data, checkout_lines)

...
def _match_lines_data_to_locked_lines(checkout_lines_data, checkout_lines):
    """Point input lines at the lines that exist now that the checkout is locked.

    The input lines are resolved against the checkout lines before the checkout
    row lock is taken, so a concurrent request may have created a line for the
    same variant in the meantime. Without this step both requests would create
    their own line for the variant instead of merging into one.
    """
    lines_by_variant_id: dict[str, list[CheckoutLine]] = defaultdict(list)
    for line in checkout_lines:
        lines_by_variant_id[str(line.variant_id)].append(line)

    for line_data in checkout_lines_data:
        if line_data.line_id or line_data.force_new_line or not line_data.variant_id:
            continue
        matching_lines = lines_by_variant_id[str(line_data.variant_id)]
        # When the variant is already in multiple lines a new line is created,
        # which mirrors the resolution done before the lock was taken.
        if len(matching_lines) == 1:
            line_data.line_id = str(matching_lines[0].pk)
notes: Commit message describes the mechanism in detail. Backport; original PR #19889. Fix is a squash-merge commit; merge_commit = that commit.

title: Nested list pagination reports hasPreviousPage=false on page 2
symptom: Nested connections (e.g. me { orders }) say there is no previous page when paginating forward with a cursor, unlike root connections.
root_cause: Two pagination code paths implement page-info rules differently (strict Relay vs lenient).
trigger: first + after on a list-backed (dataloader) connection.
why_missed: Both paths follow 'a' spec; the inconsistency is only visible comparing them.
fix_summary: Set has_previous_page/has_next_page in the list path the same way as the queryset path.
pattern: two implementations of one contract drift apart
fixed:
# This function handles pagination for list-based data (e.g., from dataloaders).
    # The graphql-relay `connection_from_list_slice` follows the strict Relay
    # spec where `has_previous_page` is only set when using `last` and
    # `has_next_page` only when using `first`. Our queryset-based pagination
    # (`connection_from_queryset_slice` → `_get_page_info`) is more lenient:
    # it sets `has_previous_page = True` whenever an `after` cursor is present
    # (forward pagination) and `has_next_page = True` whenever a `before` cursor
    # is present (backward pagination). Align the list path with the queryset
    # path so that nested connection fields (e.g., `me { orders }`) behave
    # consistently with root-level connections.
    first = args.get("first")
    last = args.get("last")
    after = args.get("after")
    before = args.get("before")
    if first and after:
        slice.page_info.has_previous_page = True
    if last and before:
        slice.page_info.has_next_page = True
notes: Symptom paraphrased from the PR title, commit message and added test; the linked issue thread was not read. Fix is a squash-merge commit; merge_commit = that commit.
